Subject: MSA & Order Form — sequencing signer plan for capacity uplift

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we can keep momentum on the 18-month renewal + capacity uplift:

- You confirmed target start date of 2027-08-01 for increased capacity (additional 4 GPU units).
- Your legal team will return redlines to the MSA and updated order form by EOD Wednesday.
- We need an execution path that avoids pausing production (staggered signers: procurement then finance then final signature).

Attached is a clean order form template and a suggested exhibit sequencing doc (OrderForm_Uplift_2027-06-30.pdf). If your legal team prefers tracked changes, we can accept a redline doc — happy to coordinate.

Can you confirm who on your side will approve billing changes vs. commercial terms? If procurement signs first, we will schedule the DocuSign envelope in two stages to preserve the old capacity until the uplift effective date.

Thanks,
Markus

Hi Markus —

Appreciate the summary. Legal returned an MSA with tracked redlines, and procurement attached an updated PO-ready order form. Please see attached: Ava_MSARedline_2027-06-30.docx and OrderForm_Uplift_2027-06-30.pdf.

Key open points from our side (high-level):
1) Liability cap language — legal requested proportional cap tied to the new annual commitment rather than prior term.
2) Data retention clause — need explicit audit log retention window (we asked for 24 months).
3) Billing effective date — procurement wants the uplift charges to start on the signature date, not the service start date.

Procurement will sign the order form first (they prefer), then legal will finish the MSA loop. Finance will countersign after we confirm billing timings. Can you confirm Redwood’s ability to provide a log export for 24 months?

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Director of Partnerships, Ava Innovations
samir.rao@avainnov.com

Attachments: Ava_MSARedline_2027-06-30.docx; OrderForm_Uplift_2027-06-30.pdf

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MSA redlines from Ava Innovations — quick legal triage

Team — forwarding Samir’s redlines. I reviewed the doc and flagged the high-priority items inline. Summary of my read:

- Liability cap: ask for a compromise — propose carve for uptime/SLA credits and keep general cap at 12 months of fees for the renewal term; commercial can offer credit-sizing for the uplift.
- Data retention/audit logs: we can provide 24 months of audit log export as a one-time deliverable and suggest an operational export arrangement (automated daily dumps to their S3) as part of a professional services addendum.
- Billing effective date: we should align billing to the effective service date to avoid retroactive credits; propose a phased start (procurement signs to schedule, billing starts on 2027-08-01).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Markus to confirm commercial willingness on phased billing and credit guardrails.
2) Lauren to draft a brief addendum language for audit log exports and PS scope.
3) Mateo to prepare a DocuSign envelope plan with staged signers and a fallback (if procurement insists on signature-first billing).

Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachment: annotated_Ava_MSARedline_2027-06-30.docx (internal comments)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — sequencing signer plan for capacity uplift

Samir — quick follow-up after legal triage. We can accommodate most of the asks with the plan below:

1) Liability cap: Redwood proposes 12 months fees cap for the renewed commitment including the uplift. For operational outages tied to the new capacity, we’ll honor SLA credits as structured in Exhibit E.
2) Audit logs: Redwood will deliver a 24-month audit log export as a one-time export. If Ava would like continuous access, we can add an optional PS line item to set up automated S3 exports. I’ve asked Lauren to draft the exact addendum text.
3) Billing effective date: We agree to start billing on 2027-08-01 (service effective date). Procurement can sign the order form first to confirm quantities; the DocuSign envelope will have staged execution so finance signs after the billing start is scheduled. If procurement insists on invoicing from signature, we’ll include a one-time credit to offset retroactive charges.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Lauren: send addendum & exhibit language by Monday 07/05.
- Mateo: prepare DocuSign envelope plan and staging by EOD 07/05.
- Samir: confirm procurement sign preference and whether they need a PO number in the envelope.

If that works, I’ll coordinate the DocuSign flow and loop in Finance for the credit guardrail if needed.

Thanks,
Markus

Team —

Attached are two items for internal review: 1) a short audit-log addendum (Addendum_AuditExport_2027-07-05.docx) that commits to a one-time 24-month export and an optional PS line for S3 automation, and 2) a DocuSign sequencing plan (DocuSign_Plan_2027-07-05.pdf) that stages procurement -> finance -> final exec.

I kept the addendum minimal to avoid reopening broad MSA language: sample clause below — ready for legal polish: 

"Redwood will provide a one-time export of audit logs covering the prior twenty-four (24) months as a deliverable to Customer within thirty (30) days of the effective date. Redwood offers an optional professional services engagement to configure continuous audit log exports to Customer-controlled S3 for a separately agreed fee."

Please review so we can share with Samir today. Mateo — once we agree, can you stage the envelope with a required PO field on the procurement signer? That will satisfy their workflow.
